title: When the Vector Falls
premise: Mara Zhou smuggles memories through the quarantine cordon around Meridian Station, where a forgotten colony is dying of orbital decay and bureaucratic neglect. When the deep-space vessel Halcyon returns with its crew biologically aged backward, carrying proof that the war's founding atrocity was staged, Mara becomes the only courier both sides trust — or fear — enough to deliver it. Hunted by fleet intelligence and his own smuggler syndicate, he must choose between the found family he's built among Meridian's dying and the truth that could save millions. He delivers the message as the truce expires, forcing an armistice that saves the colony but costs him his ship, his records, and nearly his life; in the end, the family he chose rebuilds with him on the ground.
about_author: Casper Dunmore is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that never met. They write about couriers, quarantines, and the people who carry other people's truths.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Mara Zhou runs a memory-chip shipment past orbital customs aboard his aging freighter, the Long Answer, using a customs officer's grief for leverage. POV: Mara. Establishes his trade, his cynicism, and the dying colony of Meridian below him. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking quiet despair.

chapters.title: The Colony That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Mara docks at Meridian to deliver memories to settlers whose own archives are failing. We meet Ilsa Reyes, the station's stubborn doctor, and Juno, an orphaned teen Mara informally adopted. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: tenderness he refuses to name, found family forming in decay.

chapters.title: Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Fleet broadcast announces a ninety-day truce extension — the last before full war resumes with the Outer Compact. Smugglers calculate profits; Meridian calculates survival. POV: Mara, with interludes of intercepted fleet chatter. Emotional beat: dread ticking under routine.

chapters.title: A Ship Out of Deep Time
chapters.summary: The Halcyon, missing eleven years, appears at the cordon — every crew member biologically younger than when they left. Customs panics; Mara is bribed to be first aboard. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: awe curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Children Wearing Old Faces' Clothes
chapters.summary: Mara explores the Halcyon: reversed crew, logs encrypted in a naval cipher he recognizes from his military past. A young-old woman, Commander Sefa Anand, begs him to take one chip planetside. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: recognition — she knows his real name.

chapters.title: What the Chip Whispers
chapters.summary: In hiding, Mara plays the chip: evidence the war's inciting massacre was fabricated by fleet command to justify annexation. The reversal tech was their escape from conscience. POV: Mara, flashbacks to his service. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing; duty vs. truth begins.

chapters.title: Syndicate Summons
chapters.summary: Mara's boss, Vess Okonkwo, demands the chip as payment for old debts — the syndicate wants to sell it to the Compact. Mara stalls, lying badly. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: loyalty strained against self-preservation.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Diagnosis
chapters.summary: On Meridian, Ilsa reveals the colony's life support fails within the truce window regardless of the war. She asks Mara what he's carrying; he lies, and she sees it. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: love surfacing as confrontation.

chapters.title: Juno's Bargain
chapters.summary: Juno, eavesdropping, offers to fence the chip's location to protect Mara — and accidentally alerts fleet intelligence. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: adolescent loyalty causing adult catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Man Who Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Fleet interrogator Dane Corvus arrives, a former comrade who once saved Mara's life, offering amnesty for the chip. Their history complicates everything. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: old brotherhood weaponized.

chapters.title: Running the Cordon Backward
chapters.summary: Mara flees with the chip hidden inside a memory of his mother, smuggling his own past past his own scanners. Syndicate hunters and fleet ships both pursue. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: exhilarating terror; commitment to the message.

chapters.title: Vess's Price
chapters.summary: Captured by the syndicate, Mara bargains: the chip's contents freely given, not sold — truth shouldn't have a buyer. Vess, herself a colony orphan, wavers. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: persuasion as intimacy; loyalty redefined.

chapters.title: Sefa Descending
chapters.summary: Commander Anand reaches Meridian, revealing the reversal is killing the crew — they traded years for the evidence. She has days. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: sacrifice made explicit; stakes humanized.

chapters.title: Siege of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Fleet marines quarantine Meridian under pretext; Ilsa treats wounded from both sides while Juno runs supplies through maintenance shafts. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: civilian courage against machinery of war.

chapters.title: Corvus's Confession
chapters.summary: Corvus corners Mara and admits he already knows the truth — he's spent years burying it because exposure would indict everyone he loves. He offers Mara a choice: silence and safety. POV: Corvus. Emotional beat: antagonist revealed as mirror.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Nobody Authorized
chapters.summary: Juno, improvising, transmits fragments of the chip on Meridian's public band. Panic spreads through both fleets; the truce frays early. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: reckless hope igniting consequences.

chapters.title: Ninety Hours
chapters.summary: With the truce collapsing, Mara must physically deliver the full chip to the Compact delegation before fleets open fire — across a blockade, in a stolen shuttle, with Sefa dying beside him. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: resolve crystallized.

chapters.title: Crossing Fire
chapters.summary: The blockade run: Corvus lets them through at the last second, choosing truth over brotherhood's corruption. Vess's ships draw fleet fire to cover the shuttle. POV: alternating Mara/Corvus. Emotional beat: enemies choosing each other's better selves.

chapters.title: The Message Delivered
chapters.summary: Mara hands the chip to the Compact council as the ceasefire expires; both fleets stand down mid-attack order. The fabrication is verified live. War ends not with victory but with shared shame. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: catharsis — the courier's burden set down.

chapters.title: Reckoning at the Cordon
chapters.summary: Fleet command fractures; some officers surrender, others sabotage. Sefa dies peacefully, her crew's years honored. Corvus turns himself in, testifying. POV: Sefa then Corvus. Emotional beat: grief braided with justice.

chapters.title: Groundfall
chapters.summary: Meridian gets relief funding as war reparations; the Long Answer is destroyed in the final skirmish. Mara, Ilsa, and Juno descend to the colony's surface together — his first time standing on ground in nine years. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: homecoming without heroics.

chapters.title: New Memories, Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Months later, Mara runs a small honest relay station, no longer smuggling the past but transmitting the present. Ilsa rebuilds the archives; Juno trains as a signal officer. Some moments, he decides, are meant only for the people living them. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: peace chosen, family kept, truth carried forward lightly.
